buffett.question: When we lost those margin points on Synthetic Blend and Conventional Engine Oil, did we lose them because we cut price, or because the cost of the oil we buy went up and we ate it instead of passing it along?

Did we hold our volume on these five lines while margin fell, or did we lose volume too — because if price went up and volume held, that's a fine business, and if volume fell anyway, that tells us something different about what we actually sell
Are our competitors selling the same oil at the same lower price, or are we the only one giving up margin here
Since 2026-006, what actually changed — a contract renewal, a new competitor, a raw material contract, or did we make a pricing decision ourselves
Is this margin problem showing up only in the Value category, or has it started creeping into our premium synthetic lines too
If fixing this means raising prices and risking some customers walk, how much volume are you willing to lose to get the margin back, versus just living with today's margin

bezos.question: When we say gross margin is 'underperforming target,' is the target itself a fixed cost-plus number set at the start of the year, or does it flex with input commodity costs like base oil and additive prices — and if the latter, has that flex mechanism actually been triggered for 2026-006 forward?

For the five product lines in question, did we make a deliberate customer-backwards decision — for example holding price to defend share in Value while input costs rose — or is this margin decline entirely unplanned and unexplained by any pricing or promotional action we took?
Is the six-percentage-point-plus decline concentrated in a specific set of customers, channels, or geographies, or is it uniform across the entire base for each of these five product lines?

Are we comparing against a prior-year period that was itself unusually strong — for instance elevated pricing from a supply shock or a one-time input cost spike that has since normalized — such that this 'decline' is really reversion rather than deterioration?

How much margin are you personally willing to sacrifice on these five lines over the next two to three quarters if it is buying us retained or expanded share in Value and Conventional segments, versus how much of this needs to be clawed back immediately for reporting reasons?

Is the corrective action we take here reversible within a quarter — a price adjustment or promotional pullback — or are we contemplating something structural like renegotiating supplier contracts or reformulating products, which we cannot easily unwind once started?

musk.question: What is the raw material cost (base oil, additives, packaging) per unit for each of these five products today versus 2026-006, and what fraction of the margin decline is pure input cost inflation we failed to pass through?
Who approved the current pricing/discount structure for the Value category and Synthetic Blend/Conventional lines, and do they still believe those terms are correct given the margin erosion?

Are we buying base oil, additives, and packaging through a common supplier contract across all five lines, or are these five separate procurement chains with five separate negotiated rates and no shared leverage?
What specifically changed in 2026-006 — supplier contract, formulation, freight, customer mix, or competitor pricing — and why did none of that trigger a price/cost review until now?
What is the minimum acceptable gross margin percentage for each of these five lines individually, and are we willing to lose volume/customers to hold that floor?
If we fixed only the highest-leverage line first, which one, and what's the real deadline before this compounds into next quarter's numbers?

ohno.question: Have you walked the line where these five oils are blended and filled since June, or is this margin number your first look at the process?
What changed at the actual operation—supplier, formulation, fill line, shift—in the month margin broke, 2026-006?
When you say margin declined, is that price falling or cost per unit rising—have you stood at the point where the cost enters the product and seen which?
Do Synthetic Blend and Conventional Engine Oil share the same base oil supplier or the same blending tank as Compressor, Hydraulic, and Manual Gear Oil?
Against which prior period do you judge 'target'—last year's actual, or a plan set before the base oil market moved?
If the root cause is a defect condition upstream, are you prepared to stop shipping those five lines until it is found, or must the line keep running regardless of what we find?

verdict: NO EVIDENCE (indistinguishable from random tagging) -> stop; close Stage I at B-2
